assign.request: Reviewer minion for /imagine/generated/: ten-second test, primary interaction, layout at 3440, resolve findings in-realm, land.
steps: read realm-alternates task.jsonl + critique row (width already fixed today)

log.msg: Ten-second test at 1280 (before any fix). STRANGER: a settings-ish detail page titled 'Generated' with a dense jargon paragraph (generator, page.js, children:, width words) and one small card, 'Seed 7', floating alone in a mostly-empty page - looks like an empty or broken admin screen, not clear what a 'seed' is or what to do with it. MEANT (page.js description + readme.md): page trees exported from the page generator, landed as real editable page.js files - export a tree there, it appears here as a directory you then edit. The two sentences differ mainly on WHY there's only one lonely card - the meant text never said, so a stranger reads emptiness as breakage rather than 'early, more coming'.

Primary interaction: the only clickable thing on the 1280 shot is the 'Seed 7' card. ui-test plan (generated-plan.json) clicked '.page--generated .page-preview-link' and it does exactly what the label promises - opens a new 'Seed 7' column at /imagine/generated/seed-7/ (confirmed via location.href + DOM text, since .page.column is display:contents so its own getBoundingClientRect reads 0x0 by design, not a bug - had to probe href/scrollWidth/innerText instead of trusting the watched rect). NOT a broken-control finding. But one level in, the Seed 7 column (before fix) showed only two bare links with zero explanation: 'Journal' -> /imagine/generated/seed-7/vtabs/ and 'Backlog' -> /imagine/generated/seed-7/list/. Traced both: vtabs/page.js declares title:'Journal' (it's actually a vertical tab rail, ext/tabs), list/page.js declares title:'Backlog' (it's actually a plain core column list). Confirmed by reading source, not a state-leak bug - the page generator just seeds each exported page with a generic flavor-text title unrelated to its structural directory name, and nothing on screen said so. That mismatch, at the very next click after the lonely card, is the sharper version of the emptiness complaint: a stranger who does get past 'Seed 7' lands on two made-up words with no clue they're placeholders.

Layout at 3440 - width already fixed today, not redone. Critique row (public/imagine/paging/critique/page.js, REALMS[1]): '29% wide - 2180px dead - depth 6 - scroll 1392/1392', weak: one Seed 7 card floats alone in a 40em rail with 2180px of blank paper, the emptiest screen in the set. realm-alternates/task.jsonl (landed 17:47 today) applied width:'large' (not the critique's suggested 'wide', because 'fill'/'wide'-style flex-basis was measured to squeeze a column opened under seed-7 to its 288px floor and overflow the row 11-16%, tested on this exact realm's seed-7/vtabs/prose/) and re-measured: front at 3440 went 36.6%/2180px dead -> 46%/1856px dead; at 1280, 63.4%/468px dead -> 91.6%/107px dead. Deep in the tree (seed-7/vtabs/prose) at 3440 with large: 94% used, 380px dead, no overflow. Re-verified myself at 1280/3440 post my own content edits: still true, nothing regressed - the applied alternate stands, not reverted. Three layout invariants hold on both my before/after 3440 shots: nothing at x:0 (nav rail starts the row, which is the shared /imagine/ shell on every realm, not this realm's content; the actual prose starts ~280px in), no text line runs past the ~40em measure (paragraph column width unchanged by my content edits, still clamped by the shared prose class), no hand-typed spacing constant (this realm has zero CSS files of its own - only page.js + readme.md - so nothing to check).

action.msg: Added a clause to content(): names the 'tree' concept in plain words, and explicitly says only one has been exported so far so the single card reads as early, not broken - answers the critique's own framing ('the emptiest screen in the set') directly on the page instead of leaving a reader to guess. Caveat: assumes the realm stays this sparse a while longer; once several seeds exist, the 'only one so far' clause should come out (it would then read as stale, not wrong) - easy one-line revert.

Added a content() with a takeaway sentence - the highest-value fix in the brief's own priority order, and this page had none at all: it was a bare title over two unexplained links. New sentence defines 'seed' in plain words, then names the exact mismatch found in the primary-interaction test - Journal is really vtabs/ (a vertical tab rail), Backlog is really list/ (a plain column list) - so a reader gets the real shape before clicking through jargon. Caveat: assumes 'Journal'/'Backlog' stay as the generator's placeholder titles; if a person later edits vtabs/page.js or list/page.js to a real title, this sentence goes stale and should be cut or reworded to match - it is one paragraph, cheap to revisit. Did NOT touch vtabs/page.js, list/page.js or anything under them (same placeholder-title pattern recurs at wall/tabs/prose leaves three levels down - e.g. vtabs/wall/page.js:'Queue', list/wall/page.js:'Register') - the readme.md explicitly frames the whole export as raw scaffold a person is meant to overwrite, and the leaf pages already say so honestly ('The end of a branch - this is where the real page goes.'), so scrubbing every placeholder title would fight the demo's own point rather than help it. Logged as PROPOSED below instead of edited everywhere.

log.msg: Correction to the previous entry's last line: the deeper placeholder-title pattern (Queue, Register, Atlas, etc. three levels down) is not a core/ext proposal - it's fully inside my fences, a real page.js edit I could make. I chose not to, for the design-intent reason given (readme.md + leaf comments already frame it as scaffold meant to be overwritten), which is a 'left open with a reason', not a park. If the owner disagrees, the fix is the same one-line-content() pattern applied at seed-7/page.js, repeated at each wall/tabs page - mechanical, no core change needed.

shot.note: zero console errors at either width on either url (drive.mjs + a separate networkidle Playwright script both report none); final 1280 keeper copied to /framework/ai/2026-09-04/imagine-review/shots/generated.jpg, 45.6KB jpeg quality 70

assign.outcome:
**Fixed the clarity gap the critique named, one click deep.** The width fix (`width: "large"`, shipped earlier today by `realm-alternates`) stands untouched and re-confirmed: 3440 dead space 36.6%/2180px → 46%/1856px, 1280 dead space 63.4%/468px → 91.6%/107px — not re-measured from scratch, not reverted. What was still broken was clarity, not width: [`/imagine/generated/`](/imagine/generated/) now says *why* there's only one card (only one tree exported so far, more queue up as they export), and [`/imagine/generated/seed-7/`](/imagine/generated/seed-7/) — which had **zero** on-page explanation before this task, just a title over two bare links — now tells a reader that *Journal* and *Backlog* are the generator's placeholder names for a vertical tab rail (`vtabs/`) and a plain column list (`list/`), traced and confirmed by reading both files' `title:` fields.

The primary interaction (click the Seed 7 card) already worked correctly — it opens the right column at the right url — the finding was that what it opened next was unexplained, not broken.

**Left as-is, with a reason:** the same generator-placeholder-title pattern (`Queue`, `Register`, `Atlas`, …) recurs three levels deeper. Not fixed — the realm's own readme.md and the leaf pages' own comments ("this is where the real page goes") already frame the whole export as raw scaffold meant to be overwritten by hand; scrubbing every placeholder title would fight that design intent rather than serve it. Same one-line `content()` pattern would apply if the owner disagrees.

Zero console errors at 1280 or 3440, before or after.
